standard_prerequisites.name: Cut
standard_prerequisites.statement: A cut is a subset alpha of the rationals that is non-empty and proper, initial (if p < q and q is in alpha then p is in alpha) and has no greatest element; the reals are the cuts.
standard_prerequisites.use: The proof verifies exactly these three clauses for the union of the family (923-936) and uses them for the members of the family when it passes from p < q in the union to p in the union.

standard_prerequisites.name: Order on cuts
standard_prerequisites.statement: For cuts alpha and beta, alpha is at most beta exactly when alpha is a subset of beta.
standard_prerequisites.use: Upper bound and least upper bound are read through this order in the second half of the proof (937-938).

standard_prerequisites.name: Union of a family of sets
standard_prerequisites.statement: The union of a family S is the set of p that belong to some member alpha of S.
standard_prerequisites.use: The candidate supremum is defined as the union of S, and both halves of the proof unpack membership in it (920-921, 930-935, 938).

core_obligations: Let S be any non-empty set of cuts with an upper bound and put lambda equal to the union of S (920-921).

Show lambda is non-empty and proper: a member of S supplies an element, S being a set of cuts makes lambda a subset of the rationals, and a rational absent from every member of S is absent from lambda (925-929).
Show lambda is initial: if p < q and q is in lambda then q lies in some cut alpha of S, so p lies in alpha and hence in lambda (930-932).
Show lambda has no greatest element: if p lies in lambda then p lies in some cut alpha of S, which has an element q above p, and that q lies in lambda (933-935).
Conclude lambda is a cut and an upper bound of S, since every member of S is a subset of the union (936-937).

Show minimality: if beta is a cut containing every member of S and p lies in lambda, then p lies in some member of S and hence in beta, so lambda is a subset of beta and lambda is the least upper bound (938).

proof_roadmap.step: Take the union of the family as the candidate least upper bound.
Verify the three clauses of the definition of a cut for that union.
Read off that the union is an upper bound of the family.
Show every upper bound of the family contains the union, so the union is least.

difficulty_reason: Counted unit is the author's theorem at source lines 915-917: the set of cuts has the Completeness Property, spelled out four lines earlier as the assertion that every non-empty set of cuts with an upper bound has a least upper bound (908-913). The 21-line proof constructs the candidate supremum as the union of the family and then discharges the three clauses of the definition of a cut for that union (923-936) before showing it is an upper bound and the least one (937-938). The definition of a cut is used clause by clause, and the minimality half has to pass between membership in the union and membership in a member of the family, so the argument is not a one-line consequence of the definitions.
